before.title: 0.9/1.2 TCe Timing Chain Premature Stretch and Tensioner/Guide Failure
before.description: Both the 0.9 TCe 90 (H4Bt) and 1.2 TCe 120 (H5Ft) petrol engines use a nominally 'lifetime' timing chain that in practice can stretch prematurely from around 80,000-100,000 km, with weak tensioners and plastic guides that crack or snap. A contributing root cause is the small oil jet that lubricates the chain, which clogs with soot when oil changes are stretched, accelerating chain and sprocket wear. Owners on UK forums report rattles followed by snapped guides and slipped chains, which can leave the car a non-starter or cause valve damage.
before.solution: Replace the complete timing chain kit (chain, tensioner, guides and sprockets) at the first sign of rattle, and verify the chain oil jet is clear during the job. Strict, shortened oil change intervals with the correct specification oil are the accepted prevention; Renault has contributed goodwill (e.g. 75%) on some out-of-warranty failures.
symptoms: Metallic rattle from the engine on cold start
Ticking/rattling from the timing cover area that worsens with revs
Loss of power accompanied by engine warning light
Crank/cam correlation fault codes stored
Engine cranks but won't start after chain slips

before.title: 1.2 TCe (H5Ft) Excessive Oil Consumption — "Motorgate" Piston Ring Defect
before.description: Captur I models with the 1.2 TCe 120 (H5Ft) engine built between 2012 and mid-2016 suffer a manufacturing defect: tolerances between the pistons, piston rings and cylinder walls are too wide, letting engine oil pass into the combustion chamber and burn. Affected cars can consume 1 litre of oil per 1,000-1,500 km, fouling the catalytic converter and exhaust valves, and in the worst cases starving the engine of oil and causing failure as early as 40,000-60,000 km. Over 400,000 vehicles across Europe are affected; the French "Motorgate" class action and a DGCCRF investigation target Renault over this engine, which the company corrected in production in May 2016 but never formally recalled.
before.solution: Renault's procedure is an ECU software update that raises intake manifold pressure to reduce oil ingestion; if consumption remains above 0.25 L/1,000 km the piston rings must be replaced, and severely worn engines need a rebuild or replacement. Owners should check oil every 1,000 km, keep documented top-up records to support goodwill claims, and avoid 2012-2016 cars without service history.
symptoms: Oil level drops noticeably between services (up to 1L per 1,000-1,500 km)
Low oil pressure or oil level warning light
Blue smoke from exhaust, especially on startup
Misfires and rough running from oil-fouled plugs
Loss of power or sudden engine failure in severe cases

before.title: 1.5 dCi DPF/EGR Clogging and AdBlue SCR Faults on Short-Trip Cars
before.description: The 1.5 dCi (K9K) diesel Captur is prone to diesel particulate filter clogging when used mainly for short urban journeys that never let the filter complete an active regeneration; the EGR valve typically sools up at the same time, compounding the airflow restriction. After repeated failed regenerations the ECU forces limp mode with 'Check Anti-Pollution System' warnings. On later Euro 6d Blue dCi versions, AdBlue/SCR faults — injector crystallisation, NOx sensor errors and incorrect urea level readings — additionally trigger 'No start in xxx km' countdown restrictions.
before.solution: A forced regeneration via diagnostic tool or a professional DPF clean usually restores a clogged filter, with EGR valve cleaning or replacement done at the same time; fully blocked filters or failed SCR components (injector, NOx sensor) must be replaced. Prevention is a 20-30 minute sustained-speed motorway run every 300-400 km of urban use and keeping AdBlue topped up with fresh fluid.
symptoms: 'Check Anti-Pollution System' message with engine warning light
Reduced power / limp mode
Frequent active regenerations (raised idle, cooling fan, hot smell)
Rising fuel consumption
AdBlue warning with 'No start in xxx km' countdown (Blue dCi models)

before.title: Cabin Water Ingress Through Door Seals and Blocked Sill Drains
before.description: First-generation Capturs commonly let rainwater into the cabin, most often soaking the rear footwells. The root causes documented across owner forums are thin rear door seals that detach or fail, a poorly designed seal between the bulkhead and the sills, and sill drain (weep) holes that block with dirt — once a sill fills with water it overflows into the floorpan. Left unfixed, standing water under the carpets causes damp smells, persistent window misting, corrosion and faults in underfloor wiring and modules.
before.solution: Trace the entry point with a hose test, then re-seat or replace the failed door weatherstrips, clear the sill weep holes and rubber bungs, and reseal the bulkhead-to-sill joint where needed. Carpets and underlay must be lifted and fully dried to protect wiring and prevent mould.
symptoms: Soaking wet rear passenger footwell carpet after rain
Damp, musty smell and windows misting up inside
Water heard sloshing in the sills or found under sill bungs
Water dripping from the door trim or seal when opening the door
Electrical gremlins from moisture under the carpets

before.title: E-Tech Hybrid Gearbox Input-Shaft O-Ring Oil Leak (155,825-Vehicle Recall)
before.description: On Captur II E-Tech hybrid and plug-in hybrid models, a faulty O-ring seal on the hollow primary shaft of the electric motor inside the DB1 multimode gearbox allows gearbox oil to leak internally. Leaking oil first damages the temperature sensor and, in severe cases, contaminates and overheats the electric motor, causing loss of power or complete loss of drive, with out-of-warranty repairs running €3,000-8,000 for a motor or gearbox replacement. Renault recalled 155,825 E-Tech hybrids built between 5 April 2019 and 26 September 2022 (Clio 5, Captur 2, Arkana, Mégane 4, Dacia Jogger) to check the seal.
before.solution: Under the recall, dealers leak-test the hollow primary shaft seal and replace the original O-ring with an improved X-ring seal free of charge (about 30 minutes if no damage has occurred). If oil has already contaminated the electric motor or sensor, the affected components or the complete gearbox must be replaced; cars built after September 2022 have the improved seal from the factory.
symptoms: Gearbox fault or 'Electrical Failure Danger' warning on dashboard
Sudden loss of power or loss of drive while driving
Powertrain overheating warning
Oil traces under the gearbox/electric motor area
Jerky or inconsistent gear changes from the multimode gearbox

before.title: Electronic Parking Brake Fails to Auto-Engage — Actuator Sensor Recall (RAPEX 37/2025)
before.description: Captur II vehicles built between 10 April 2024 and 16 January 2025 are covered by an EU safety recall (RAPEX alert 37/2025, ref. SR/03262/25) for an incorrectly angled position sensor inside the electronic parking brake actuator. The misaligned sensor can place the stopping pin incorrectly, so the parking brake does not properly engage when the driver presses P, switches off the engine, releases the seatbelt or opens the door — creating a risk of the vehicle rolling away. The same defect affects the Renault Austral, Mégane E-Tech, Scenic E-Tech, Espace VI and Rafale; the backup Assisted Parking Brake function remains operational.
before.solution: This is a free safety recall: dealers inspect the actuator position sensor alignment and stop-pin position and perform the prescribed corrective action or software update. Owners of affected VINs are contacted by Renault; until the fix, leaving the car in gear and confirming the brake indicator illuminates is advised.
symptoms: Parking brake does not engage automatically when P is selected or engine is switched off
Parking brake warning indicator fails to illuminate after parking
Vehicle creeps or rolls when parked on a slope
Parking brake fault message on instrument cluster
